questions.question: A workstation opens an SSH session to one router's individual IPv4 address. Which delivery type is it?

option_explanations.A: Loopback stays on the originating host.
option_explanations.C: Broadcast addresses every receiver in its broadcast scope.
option_explanations.D: Multicast addresses a group rather than one individual address.

questions.question: Which destination is the IPv4 limited broadcast address?
questions.explanation: Limited broadcast targets the local broadcast domain and routers do not forward it.

option_explanations.A: 0.0.0.0 denotes an unspecified IPv4 address in this context.
option_explanations.C: Limited broadcast targets the local broadcast domain and routers do not forward it.
option_explanations.D: 224.0.0.1 is the all-hosts group on the local multicast link.

questions.question: Which delivery type addresses a group of interested receivers?
questions.explanation: Multicast addressing represents a group rather than a particular receiver.

option_explanations.A: Multicast addressing represents a group rather than a particular receiver.
option_explanations.B: Limited broadcast targets the entire local broadcast scope.

questions.question: A frame capture shows destination ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff and EtherType 0x0806. What is the delivery scope of that frame?

options.C: Only stations subscribed to a multicast group
options.D: Every routed subnet that has an ARP entry

questions.explanation: The all-ones destination MAC makes this ARP frame a link-layer broadcast.

option_explanations.A: A switch floods the Ethernet broadcast rather than consulting one learned port.
option_explanations.B: The all-ones destination MAC makes this ARP frame a link-layer broadcast.
option_explanations.C: The all-ones MAC is broadcast, regardless of group membership.
option_explanations.D: Routers do not forward ordinary Ethernet broadcasts across subnets.

questions.question: For IPv4 subnet 198.51.100.64/26, which address is its directed broadcast?
questions.explanation: A /26 block spans 64 addresses. The all-ones host portion makes .127 the subnet broadcast.

option_explanations.A: .64 has all host bits clear and identifies the subnet.
option_explanations.B: A /26 block spans 64 addresses. The all-ones host portion makes .127 the subnet broadcast.
option_explanations.C: .126 is the last usable host, one below broadcast.

questions.question: Which destination falls in the IPv4 multicast address range?
A video sender has multiple interested receivers and multicast forwarding is available. What can multicast save on a shared upstream link?

options.A: It removes the need for IP addresses
options.B: It sends one independent upstream copy per receiver
options.C: It can carry a single copy before traffic branches
options.D: It changes every receiver into a broadcast source

questions.explanation: Multicast forwarding can replicate the packet at branching points instead of carrying each receiver's copy upstream.

option_explanations.A: Multicast still uses a destination IP group address.
option_explanations.B: Independent copies describe per-receiver unicast traffic.
option_explanations.C: Multicast forwarding can replicate the packet at branching points instead of carrying each receiver's copy upstream.
option_explanations.D: Receivers join groups without becoming broadcast sources.

questions.question: A DHCP client initially sends a limited broadcast on one LAN. What lets a server on another subnet handle it?

options.A: A DHCP relay configured for that LAN
options.C: A static ARP entry for the server on the client

questions.explanation: A relay receives the local discovery and forwards DHCP information to the remote server.

option_explanations.A: A relay receives the local discovery and forwards DHCP information to the remote server.
option_explanations.B: Recalculating the Ethernet checksum does not relay a DHCP message.
option_explanations.C: The initial client broadcast does not use a static neighbor entry to address a remote server.
option_explanations.D: DHCP rides on UDP rather than TCP.

questions.question: Refer to the three destination addresses in the exhibit. Which order classifies their traffic types?
questions.explanation: 192.0.2.88 can identify one endpoint, 239.10.10.10 is a group, and the all-ones address is limited broadcast.

option_explanations.A: 239.10.10.10 is multicast and the final all-ones address is broadcast, so this swaps the last two.
option_explanations.B: 192.0.2.88 is a unicast address, and the second address is multicast.
option_explanations.C: The first address is unicast and the last address is the limited broadcast, so this reverses those roles.
option_explanations.D: 192.0.2.88 can identify one endpoint, 239.10.10.10 is a group, and the all-ones address is limited broadcast.

questions.question: Two interfaces each face their own IPv4 LAN. One LAN sends ordinary Ethernet broadcasts. What additional behavior is needed for an application to convey its broadcast-discovered information across the router?

options.A: A common Ethernet link speed across both LANs
options.B: Matching frame checksums on both interfaces
options.C: A shared Ethernet destination field in both hosts' routing tables
options.D: An explicitly supported relay or application mechanism

questions.explanation: Ordinary local broadcasts stop at the router. A service-specific relay can carry selected information across the boundary.

option_explanations.A: A common link speed does not extend a broadcast domain across routed interfaces.
option_explanations.B: Each FCS verifies its own frame and cannot propagate discovery.
option_explanations.C: Routing tables select next hops and do not carry a shared destination MAC field.
option_explanations.D: Ordinary local broadcasts stop at the router. A service-specific relay can carry selected information across the boundary.
